title: A bare JSON number pasted as the response is not silently a clean BidResponse

browser.toastMatch: The bid response pane must hold a JSON object — got number

specNotes: OpenRTB 2.6 §4.2.1 defines BidResponse as an object carrying `id` and either `seatbid[]` or `nbr`. A bare JSON number satisfies neither the object requirement nor any documented vendor feed shape (every vendor response dialect in this corpus is an object or an array, never a scalar).

`rawResponse` is used rather than `replaceResponse` because the patch schema restricts `replaceResponse` to object/array/null; a scalar root can only be expressed as raw transport text. The raw text "42" is valid JSON (a number), so this is NOT a `parse: invalid-json` case — it reaches Core as a real, if non-object, value.

Confirmed directly against the running server (not inferred): posting {bidReq: <this base request>, bidRes: 42} returns HTTP 200, `validation.status: 'clean'` with only the request's own `version.assumed` finding, and `crosscheck: []` — the numeric response is dropped before it reaches any response-shaped check.
The browser correctly rejects this scalar root before transport; the exact shape rejection, zero Analyze POSTs and absence of stale results are checked independently of HTTP DEF-300.
